title: King's Indian Defense: Four Pawns Attack
line: White takes all the center it can, and Black attacks the pawns before they settle.

steps.text: The King's Indian, and White pushes a fourth pawn forward. It takes all the space it can.
Castle first. Your king is safe behind the bishop.
Strike at the center at once with the pawn on c7. White's pawns are far forward and hard to guard.
Now attack the pawn on d5 with another pawn.
Trade it off. The file that pawn stood on opens for your rook.
Put a rook on the open file. It aims down the file at White's pawn on e4.
steps.after: White pushes the pawn on, to chase your knight.

steps.text: Jump the knight forward, out of the attack. It hits the pawn on e5.

wrong.f6d7: The knight steps back. White keeps its pawns in the center and gets to attack first.

steps.after: Your knight, rook and bishop all attack the pawn, and White's center starts to fall apart.

summary: Against a center of four pawns, Black strikes at once from the side, opens a file and attacks the pawns in front.
